recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-25042; if a similar failure recurs, it should be handled as a validator/HAPI FHIR implementation issue rather than a spec source correction.
issue_request: FHIR-25042 was Published/Persuasive for FHIR-core after being raised against STU3 and applied for R5. It reported that QA/validator output rejected a DiagnosticReport containing two contained Observations where one contained Observation.derivedFrom referenced the other with a local # reference; Jira comments later classified the remaining problem as tooling-specific and the reporter confirmed the validator was OK.
initial_application: No source commit explicitly tagged FHIR-25042 was found. The relevant source behavior was already present through commit c26d2b6172e66e1f867d4ca766dc977cdcc95d5a, which changed ref-1 from %resource.contained.id to %rootResource.contained.id. Later ref-1 commits d87b97a367412efef9c243585bd036f4546fb9c5 and d0d047e3b0ef986cdd8729e4c9ad26ab903bac7f preserved that contained-to-contained lookup while adding adjacent behavior.
additional_context: Reference is an active datatype in source/fhir.ini and DomainResource is an active normative resource. Current references.html says contained resources share the parent internal id resolution space and may be referenced by something in the same container, potentially another contained resource. Adjacent contained-reference issues FHIR-31732 and FHIR-29408 already have no-change audits on the combined branch, and no relevant Zulip or Confluence conflict was found.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current active Reference ref-1 expression uses %rootResource.contained.id for local reference validation, so the current FHIR core source already conveys the behavior needed for the reported contained Observation-to-contained Observation reference.
